minimal_missing_theorem.target: For every complex Banach E, open O⊆C, f:C→E differentiable on O, and finite represented closed cycle Γ with traceΓ⊆O: if indΓ(w)=0 for all w outside O, then Γ.lineIntegral f=0. Define indΓ(w)=(2πi)^(-1)*Γ.lineIntegral(z↦(z-w)^(-1)) for w off trace, and prove its geometric winding interpretation.
minimal_missing_theorem.not_allowed_shortcut: Do not add the general Cauchy conclusion or canonical h(T)=chosen integral as a theorem premise/certificate and call full HFC closed.

canonical_independence_reduction: Represent signed difference Γ−Γ0 via finite union with reversed curves, proving additivity and index subtraction.
For fixed T, O=U\spectrum(T) is open and h(z)resolvent(T,z) is Banach-holomorphic on O.
Admissibility gives index(Γ−Γ0)=0 off O: outside U both indices0; on spectrum(T) both indices1.
General-cycle Cauchy then gives equality of chosen Dunford integrals.
Separately construct at least one admissible cycle around compact spectrum inside arbitrary U, including empty-spectrum/zero-space cases, to define canonical h(T).
executable_build_route: Bridge AC/BV represented curves to curveIntegral; prove primitive chain rule/FTC for AC paths and local primitives from Poincare.
Use compact path trace and Lebesgue subdivision to replace each curve piece by polygon segments inside convex balls while preserving integral and index.
Build finite planar polygonal/square-chain decomposition with coefficients given by winding on complementary cells. Prove its boundary equals the polygonal cycle.
Apply rectangle/triangle local Cauchy to each cell; zero winding off O ensures only cells contained in O contribute.
Derive the general-cycle Cauchy theorem, then canonical independence and admissible-cycle existence.
first_unproved_step_after_parameterizati: Finite subdivision replacement is a plausible local lemma using primitives, but no checked implementation here. The decisive missing global lemma is planar zero-winding cycle decomposition/homology. Zero winding does not imply null-homotopy (commutator loops in multiply punctured domains), so C2 homotopy invariance alone cannot substitute for homological Cauchy.
rejected_narrowing: One circle enclosing both spectra would require holomorphy across holes and can fail for general U.
Convex U or global primitive narrows theorem.
Entire h or polynomial approximation alone does not cover general holomorphic h near disconnected spectra.
